Subject Rent Reduction Movement

Made by and Forwarded by D.I. Everest

The movement for a reduction of rent first came to
the attention of the Police in March, 1932, when local
agitators formed an organization known as the "Shanghai
Citizens' Rent Reduction and Exemption Movement Committee."
This body established an office at 101 Chihli Road, but soon
afterwards went out of existence for lack of support. The
agitation was revived in the early part of 1934 when local
public bodies established the "Shanghai Municipality Rent
Reduction Movement Committee" and the "2nd Special District
Rent Reduction Movement Association."

From the beginning of 1934, the Rent Reduction Movement
steadily gained strength, and became firmly established when
the (1) "Shanghai Municipality Nantao District Rent Reduction
Committee," (2) the "1st Special District Citizens' Rent
Reduction Association" and (3) the "Federation of Rent Reduction
Movement Committees in Various Districts in Shanghai" were
organized. The first of these was formed in June, 1934 and the
second and third in July and August respectively of 1935.

The three organizations mentioned were founded with
the cognizance of the Kuomintang which has showed sympathy with
the agitation since it was first started, and recent decisions
by local Chinese Courts indicate that this sympathy is shared
by certain judges and magistrates. The 1st Special District
Court (Settlement) on October 17, 1935, in a suit for non-
payment of rent, ordered the plaintiffs, the Lih Dah (立達公司)
Company, 277 Ningpo Road, to reduce the rents of their property
in Lane 805, East Seward Road, by 20% retroactive from
January 1, 1935. Another case occurred in Chapei in the early
part of September, 1935, when the Nantao District Court

主题 减租运动

由警司 Everest 制作并呈报

减租运动首次引起警方注意是在1932年3月，当时当地煽动者组建了一个名为“上海市民减租免租运动委员会”的组织。该机构在直隶路101号设立了办事处，但不久后因缺乏支持而解散。1934年初，随着当地公共团体成立“上海市减租运动委员会”和“第二特区减租运动协会”，这一鼓动活动再次兴起。

从1934年初开始，减租运动稳步壮大，并在成立了(1)“上海市南市减租委员会”、(2)“第一特区市民减租协会”以及(3)“上海各区减租运动委员会联合会”后得以稳固确立。第一个组织成立于1934年6月，第二和第三个组织分别成立于1935年7月和8月。

上述三个组织的成立均得到了国民党的知晓，国民党自该运动发起之初便对其表示同情，且近期中国地方法院的判决表明，某些法官和推事也持有同样的同情态度。1935年10月17日，第一特区法院（租界）在一起欠付租金的诉讼案中，命令原告——位于宁波路277号的立達公司（Lih Dah Company）——将其位于西华德路东段805弄内的房产租金自1935年1月1日起追溯降低20%。另一起案件发生在1935年9月初的闸北，当时南市法院

        The growth in the strength of the movement, which has
been accelerated by the depression, the sympathy of the
Kuomintang and the favourable Court decision have emboldened
the leaders of the movement, who now aim at securing a
general decrease in Shanghai rents by 40%.
        The increasing truculence of the agitators is illustrated
in an article published in the Sin Wan Pao on October 22, 1935.
The writer, one Chu Ying ( 朱英 ), suggests that landlords
should submit to their tenants particulars of the area and
value of the land on which the houses are built, the cost of
the buildings, average cost of taxes, insurance, water rate,
repairs, etc.    Having secured these details the tenants
should decide on the amount of rent to be paid, allowing
reasonable interest on the landlord's outlay.  The article
concludes by stating that the Settlement and Chinese
Authorities should organize a joint committee of arbitration
to deal with rent disputes.

particular lane or alleyway.  The most influential Rent
Reduction Organization in the Settlement is the "First Special

        在经济萧条、国民党的同情以及有利的法院判决加速推动下，该运动的力量日益增长，这鼓舞了运动领袖，他们现在的目标是将上海的租金普遍降低40%。
        煽动者日益嚣张的气焰体现在1935年10月22日《新闻报》（Sin Wan Pao）发表的一篇文章中。作者朱英（Chu Ying）建议，房东应向租户提交房屋所占土地的面积和价值、建筑成本、平均税费、保险费、水费、维修费等明细。租户在获得这些详细信息后，应决定应付租金金额，同时允许房东的投资获得合理利息。文章最后指出，租界当局和中国当局应组织一个联合仲裁委员会来处理租金纠纷。

FRENCH CONCESSION

The "2nd Special District Rent Reduction Movement Association"
was formed on February 1, 1934, under the auspices of the "2nd
Special District Citizens' Federation," 434 Rue Auguste Boppe.
It is under the control of a lawyer named Mao Yuin (毛雲),
who is the Chairman of the 2nd District (French Concession)
Kuomintang, and eighteen committee members of the Federation.
It lacks energy and usually leaves agitation for a reduction in
rent to the tenants themselves. Five district sections have been
formed by the tenants and all of them are registered with the
parent body with the exception of one which is affiliated with
the "Nantao District Rent Reduction Movement Association." Only
three out of the five sections are now active, the remaining two
having ceased to function after securing reductions in rent.

CHAPEI
    The "Rent Reduction Movement Federation of the Hongkew
and Chapei Districts of the Shanghai Municipality" was promoted
in August, 1935, by two committee members of the Kwangtung
Fellow Countrymen's Association named Wong Deng-keng (王鈍根)
and Wu Ts-wei (吳子恆), with an office at 173 Chun Ka Zah
Road, Chapei. Shortly after its formation members of the
federation made a house-to-house visit in Chapei canvassing
for new members who were required to pay $1 each as entrance
fee. The "1st Special District Citizens' Federation," however,
complained to the local Kuomintang against the collection of
subscription fees from tenants and the federation was compelled
to close on September 11, 1935. The promoters, by no means
daunted by their failure, recommenced their activities and two
days later organized the "Rent Reduction Federation of All
Tenants in Shanghai." This movement is still in existence
and the promoters continue to collect a subscription fee of
$1 from each new member. Investigations show that the persons
connected with the aforementioned rent reduction movement have
only one idea, and that is to further their own interests.
It is of interest to note that some of the promoters were the
organizers of the now defunct "Preparatory Committee for the
Erection of a Hall in honour of General Chiang Kai Shek."
It is stated that they collected subscriptions totalling
$5,000 of which they misappropriated 90%.

of Various Districts in Shanghai" came into existence on
August 25, 1935. It was formed by a number of undesirable
elements from the Nantao and Eastern District Rent Reduction

“上海市虹口及闸北区减租运动联合会”于1935年8月由广东同乡会的两名委员王钝根 (Wong Deng-keng) 和吴子恒 (Wu Ts-wei) 发起成立，办公地点设在闸北春嘉乍路（Chun Ka Zah Road，音译）173号。成立后不久，联合会成员在闸北进行挨家挨户的走访，招募新会员，并要求每人缴纳1美元作为入会费。然而，“第一特区市民联合会”就向租户收取会费一事向当地国民党提出投诉，迫使该联合会于1935年9月11日关闭。发起人对他们的失败毫不气馁，重新开始活动，并在两天后组织了“上海全体租户减租联合会”。该运动目前仍然存在，发起人继续向每位新会员收取1美元的会费。调查显示，与上述减租运动有关的人员只有一个想法，那就是谋取私利。值得注意的是，部分发起人是现已解散的“筹建蒋介石将军纪念堂筹备委员会”的组织者。据说他们筹集了总计5,000美元的捐款，其中侵吞了90%。

Movement Associations and has an office at 13 Station Road,

At the present time there is no rent reduction movement
in Pootung. Between November, 1934 and March, 1935, however,
there existed a "Pootung Lan Nyi Doo Branch of the Nantao
District Rent Reduction Association." This branch was
controlled by Liu Zoong-fu (劉仲甫), owner of the Lee Tai
Second Hand Clothes Shop, 249 Lan Nyi Doo Road, and Wong Wu-chun
(王武均), owner of the Dong Nyi Lur (同義樓) Teashop, 230
Lan Nyi Doo Road, Pootung. It is reported that these persons
were eventually bought over by the landlords.

KIANGWAN
A rent reduction organization known as the "Kiangwan Rent
Reduction Committee" came into being in the office of the 7th
District Tangpu, 225 Station Road, Kiangwan, in April, 1933,
but closed in February, 1935, when the landlords agreed to
reduce the rents by 10% to 30%. The leaders of the movement
were Chiang Wen-sung (金文生), Chiang Dah-foong (蔣達豐),
Li Huh-ming (李洽民) and Yi Chong-yien (奚昌威), all
residents in Kiangwan.

目前浦东没有减租运动。然而，在1934年11月至1935年3月期间，存在一个“南市减租协会浦东兰尼杜（Lan Nyi Doo，音译）分会”。该分会由刘仲甫 (Liu Zoong-fu) 和王武均 (Wong Wu-chun) 控制，刘是浦东兰尼杜路249号李泰旧衣店的店主，王是浦东兰尼杜路230号同义楼茶楼的店主。据报道，这些人最终被房东收买。

江湾
一个名为“江湾减租委员会”的减租组织于1933年4月在江湾站前路225号第七区塘浦办事处成立，但在1935年2月关闭，当时房东同意减租10%至30%。运动的领导人是金文生 (Chiang Wen-sung)、蒋达丰 (Chiang Dah-foong)、李洽民 (Li Huh-ming) 和奚昌威 (Yi Chong-yien)，均为江湾居民。

Enquiries at the Chinese Estate Owners' Association,
260 Peking Road, reveal that the majority of Chinese tenants
in the Central and Western districts of the Settlement are

Made by D. S. Mac Adie Forwarded by Whouican D.S.

Nineteen members of the Settlement District
Rent Reduction Association at a meeting held in their
office, Chinese Chamber of Commerce building, North
Soochow Road, between 2p.m. and 4 p.m. April 14, passed
the following resolutions:-
1. That assistance be rendered to various sections in
their negotiation with landlords over rent disputes.
2. That a list of unoccupied houses in the Settlement
be compiled.
Resolution 2 is the outcome of a letter addressed
to the Association by the 21st Branch of the 1st Special
District Citizens' Federation. The Branch in question
holds the opinion that the fact that numerous houses
in the Settlement are left vacant is due to the high
rentals charged and requests the Association to ask
the S.M.C. to collect Municipal Rates for these houses
from the landlords should the property of the latter
remain unoccupied at the expiration of a certain period
to be set by the Council. The Branch also stipulated
as an alternative to the above measure that these
vacant premises be converted into Reformatories for
Beggars under the joint auspices of the S.M.C. and local
legal bodies.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE C. & S. B. REGISTRY. File No. 3482/1 No. 1 D Date April 7, 1934）

REPORT

Subject (in full) Rent Reduction Movement.

Made by D. S. Mac Adie Forwarded by A K Duncan D.S.J.

At 9 a.m. April 6, a number of workmen employed
by the landlords, Messrs. Lester Johnson & Morris, appeared
at the Pao Hwa Li, (宝華里) corner of East Seward and
Singkeepang Roads, and commenced to erect a bamboo fence
surrounding the block which comprises some 140 houses,
as a preparatory step to demolish the premises.
They were however prevented by the inmates from carrying
out their work. The tenants who were ordered at the
beginning of January, 1934, by the landlords to vacate
their houses, have been agitating for the rescission of the
instruction and to further this aim, they have organized
a rent reduction section with offices at No.1269 Singkeepang
Road (Vide previous reports on subject).

Between 5 and 6 p.m. April 6, some 15 persons
who claimed to be representatives of the Sing Nyi Faung
(新義坊) Alleyway, Rue Bougeat, held a meeting in the
office of the 8th Branch of the 2nd Special District
Citizens' Federation, No.9 Sung Tuh Li, Route Pere Robert,
and passed the following resolutions:-
1. That lawyer Wong Bei Yuen (王培元) be engaged as legal
advisor of the tenants in order to facilitate the
negotiation with the landlords for reduction in house
rent.
2. That the rent of the premises facing the street be
reduced by 20% and those in the alleyway by 10%
of the present rate.
3. That assistance be solicited from the 2nd Special
District Citizens' Federation and other local public
bodies in connection with the rent reduction movement.

报告

主题（全称）减租运动。

呈报人 D. S. Mac Adie 转呈人 A K Duncan D.S.J.

4月6日上午9时，业主 Lester Johnson & Morris 公司雇佣的一些工人出现在西华德东路（East Seward）与星加坡路（Singkeepang Roads）交汇处的宝华里（Pao Hwa Li），并开始围绕包含约140幢房屋的街区搭建竹篱笆，作为拆除房屋的准备步骤。
然而，他们的施工受到屋内居民的阻止。这些租户曾在1934年1月初被业主要求搬离房屋，他们一直 agitation（煽动/抗议）要求撤销该指令，并为达到此目的，他们在星加坡路1269号组织了减租分部（参见此前关于此主题的报告）。

4月6日下午5时至6时之间，约15名自称是布吉特路（Rue Bougeat）新义坊（Sing Nyi Faung）弄堂代表的人在罗伯特神父路（Route Pere Robert）宋德里（Sung Tuh Li）9号的第二特区市民联合会第八分会办事处举行会议，并通过以下决议：
1. 聘请律师王培元（Wong Bei Yuen）为租户的法律顾问，以便促进与业主就降低房租进行谈判。
2. 沿街房屋的租金在现行费率基础上降低20%，弄堂内房屋降低10%。
3. 就减租运动事宜，向第二特区市民联合会及其他地方公共团体寻求援助。

Subject (in full) Proposed Demolition of 140 Houses at East Seward Road and
Singkeipang Road Corner.
Made by and Forwarded by D.I. Wardrop.

Sir,
At the beginning of January, 1934, Messrs. Lester Johnson &
Morriss, No. 1 Kiukiang Road, served notice on the tenants of 140
houses at the North-west corner of East Seward and Singkeipang
Roads, to terminate their tenancy on 31-3-34, as they, the land-
lords, proposed to demolish and re-developpe their property.
On receipt of above notice, the tenants formed a tenants'
association, known as the Pao Hwa Li, Branch Office of the 6th.
Division of Shanghai 1st. Special District Peoples Association,
with office at No. 1269 Singkeipang Road.
Since the formation of the above association, negotiations
have been going on in order to have the notice to vacate the
premises recinded by the Company, and apparently the tenants are
under the impression that they were granted a further three months
grace.
At 9a.m. 6-4-34, a number of workmen employed by Messrs. Lester
Johnson & Morriss, appeared on the property and commenced to
erect a bamboo fence with the intention of closing the property
in and forcing the tenants to move out.
The above action was resented by the tenants, who gathered
around the workmen, causing them to cease operations.
Later, about thirty of the tenants came to the Police Station,
where they were advised not to cause any trouble, but to negotiate
with the landlords quietly for a settlement of the matter.
The Manager of Messrs. Lester Johnson & Morriss was informed
of the situation by D.O. "D", and advised that it would be better
in order to avoid any trouble, that a Court order be obtained from
the 1st. S.S.D. Court before taking any further action in the
matter. The work of erecting the bamboo fence has meantime

Subject (in full) Rent Reduction Movement

Made by D.S. Mac Adie Forwarded by W. Duncan ISJ

Two hundred and twenty representatives of local
various public bodies engaged in the rent reduction movement
held a meeting in the Chinese Chamber of Commerce, North
Soochow Road, at 3 p.m. March 30 when the following
resolutions were discussed and passed :-

1. That a delegation of sixteen members be appointed to
appeal to the Shanghai City Government at 10 a.m.
March 31 for assistance in the movement, and that should
this appeal bring forth no result, another call be made
at the same organ before April 10.

2. That the Chinese Estate Owners' Association be requested
to give a definite reply to the request for rent reduction.

3. That local property owners be requested to give a definite
answer to the request for rent reduction.

4. That the scale of rent reduction be adhered to.

5. That the National Government be requested to instruct
local judicial authorities not to accept any application
filed by local landowners in connection with the non-payment
of rentals by tenants, pending a settlement of the dispute.

6. That the Chinese Bar Association be urged not to accept
any cases from landlords in connection with the non-payment
of rentals.

7. That local journalists be urged to use their good offices
in propagating the rent reduction movement.

In compliance with the decision reached at the
meeting held on March 30, sixteen representatives of rent
reduction movement committee called at the Shanghai City
Government and interviewed Mr. O.K. Yui, Chief Secretary
of the Government. They appealed for assistance in the

The tenants of the Feng Sung Li (鳳生里),

hold a meeting in their office in the Chinese Chamber
of Commerce building, North Soochow Road, at 2 p.m.

March 3, 1934.
Morning Translation.
（批：D 3482/1）
（批：3 . 3 . 34）

Chen Pao and other local newspapers:

RENT REDUCTION MOVEMENT.

The Rent Reduction Movement Committee organized by various Chinese schools of all grades in Shanghai issued the following manifesto on March 2:-
"Due to world economic depression and bankruptcy in the farming districts of China, the industrial and commercial circles in this locality are facing ruin. However rentals of houses increase day by day despite trade depression, and the most part of the income of the people goes towards the payment of the rentals. The movement of rent reduction has met with strong support from the public.
"Local school authorities cannot pay high rentals and China's culture will suffer in consequence. Ninety per cent of the premises of local schools are leased and the annual rentals amount to thousands of dollars. In view of this, we have inaugurated the "Rent Reduction Movement Committee of Various Schools in Shanghai" to assist Chinese education. We have taken an oath to do our best in the struggle and will not rest until our object is attained. People of all circles and families of students should render us support."

The tenants in Dah Faung Li (大方里), Chengtu Road, sent the following letter to the Rent Reduction Committee yesterday:-
"Disregarding trade depression, the Dah Faung Company (大公司) has increased the monthly rentals by $12. Furthermore, the Company has filed a charge against the tenants in the Court with the intention of compelling us to remove and confiscating our key money equivalent to six months' rent. We are prepared to take action against the Company and request your Committee to support us."

The tenants in Tuh Yuin Li (得運里), Zia Zee Road and Zang An Faung (長安坊), Cho Meng Road, Nantao, yesterday formed Branches of the Nantao Branch of the Rent Reduction Committee.
A Branch in the Eastern District of the Rent Reduction Committee was organized yesterday.

The Rent Reduction Committee publishes the following notice in the advertisement columns of the "China Evening News" and other local newspapers:-
"All tenants should pay rents in accordance with the following measures approved at a meeting of representatives of various public organizations:-
1) Reduction to be enforced from January 1934.
2) Should landlords refuse to accept the reduced rents, the sums are to be deposited in banks.
3) Tenants who have owed rents for the last year should clear off the arrears in instalments within a period of one year.
4) Tenants and sub-tenants are to be accorded equal treatment in rent reduction.
5) Scales of reductions:-
10% reduction on rental for houses built before 1924.
20% " " " " 1925 to 1927.
30% " " " " 1928 to 1930.
40% " " " " between 1931 and 1933."

《申报》及其他本地报纸：

减租运动。

由上海各级华校组织的减租运动委员会于3月2日发布如下宣言：-
“由于世界经济萧条及中国农村地区破产，本地工商业界面临崩溃。然而，尽管贸易低迷，房租却日益上涨，民众收入的大部分用于支付租金。减租运动得到了公众的强烈支持。
“本地学校当局无力支付高昂租金，中国文化将因此受损。本地学校九成校舍为租赁，年租金达数千元。鉴于此，我们发起‘上海各校减租运动委员会’以协助华文教育。我们发誓尽力斗争，不达目的誓不罢休。望各界人士及学生家长给予支持。”

成都路大方里（Dah Faung Li）的租户昨日致函减租委员会：-
“大公司（Dah Faung Company）不顾贸易萧条，每月租金增加12元。此外，该公司已向法庭起诉租户，意图强迫我们搬离并没收相当于六个月租金的顶费。我们准备对公司采取行动，并请贵委员会支持我们。”

南市乍浦路（Zia Zee Road）得运里（Tuh Yuin Li）及曹孟路（Cho Meng Road）长安坊（Zang An Faung）的租户，昨日成立了减租委员会南市支会。
减租委员会东区支会于昨日成立。

减租委员会在《中华晚报》及其他本地报纸的广告栏刊登如下通告：-
“所有租户应按照各公共团体代表会议批准的以下措施缴纳租金：-
1) 减租自1934年1月起执行。
2) 若房东拒绝接受减后的租金，款项应存入银行。
3) 去年欠租的租户应在一年内分期还清欠款。
4) 租户与二房东在减租方面享有同等待遇。
5) 减租幅度：-
1924年前建造的房屋租金减少10%。
1925至1927年建造的房屋租金减少20%。
1928至1930年建造的房屋租金减少30%。
1931至1933年间建造的房屋租金减少40%。”

The Shanghai Municipality Rent Reduction Committee,
Chinese Chamber of Commerce building, North Soochow Road,
addressed on March 1 a letter to the Estate Owners' Association,
270 Peking Road, urging the landlords to voluntarily reduce
the house rent in accordance with the scale drawn up by the
Committee with a view to relieving the people from their
straitened circumstances and placing society on a sound basis.

Special District Citizens' Federation which is acting as a

direct but through the Sub-Office. It was also decided to
notify the tenants to observe the measures devised by the
Shanghai Municipality Rent Reduction Committee especially the
two, (a) rent to be paid at reduced rate with effect from
January, 1934 and (b) rents for 1933 in arrears to be refunded
in instalments payable within one year.
In consequence of non-payment of water charges
($2.00 per house per month) for the last two months by the
tenants of three houses of the Markham Li, Markham Road, the
landlords of the premises disconnected on March 1 the water
supply to the three houses in question. Seven members of the
Markham Li Rent Reduction Section held a meeting between noon
and 1 p.m. in House No.204 of the alleyway and decided to
instruct the whole body of the tenants to refrain from paying
water charges which, they alleged, were formerly included in
the house rent. During the proceedings, copies of a pamphlet

Subject (in full) Rent Reduction Movement

Made by D.S. Mac Adie Forwarded by W. Duncan D.S.

A pamphlet entitled "Advice to the Masons and
Carpenters' Union" was recently issued by various local
bodies headed by the 1st Special District Citizens' Federation.
The document apart from explaining that the aim of the rent
reduction movement is to restore trade and to better the
livelihood of the people, advises local masons and carpenters
to support, instead of opposing, the movement, as they will
also benefit by reductions in rent. It also urges the
masons and carpenters to lodge a protest with the Estate
Owners' Association against its decision to cancel all
existing building contracts.

Some fifteen persons who claimed to be representatives
of the tenants of the Soeh Sung Li (沙遜里) (Lane 62)

at 2 p.m. February 27 and formally inaugurated a rent
reduction section, Liu Zoong Ying (劉仲英), representing
the Settlement District Rent Reduction Association being also
present at the ceremony. It was decided that the landlord
of the lane be requested to reduce the rent by 10%.

Nine committee members of the 4th Branch of the 2nd
Special District Citizens' Federation, which is acting as
a Sub-Office of the French Concession Rent Reduction
Association, held a meeting in their office, 132, Rue Eugene
Bard between 8 p.m. and 9 p.m. February 27 and decided to
request the above Association to prepare posters advocating
rent reduction for exhibition in the district.

Dated 23rd February, 1934.
Building Permit: Request that landlords be refused.
We have received the following letter from the 9th Branch of this
Federation :-
"The tenants of Ziang Hsing Li, junction of Tatung Road
and Shanhaikwan Road, who are members of the Citizens' Feder-
ation, inform us that on the 22nd instant the Rent Office of
the Hung Meu Company, 43 Peking Road issued a notice requiring
them to vacate the premises before 1st March. Such pressure
is likely to precipitate a serious situation. The landlords,
under the pretext of rebuilding are forcing tenants to quit as
a countermove to the "rent reduction" agitation. The Federation
is asked to take steps against the oppression of tenants by
the landlords so that the tenants may live in peace. Prompt
action is desired."
At the 3rd Meeting of the Executive Committee of the Citizens'
Federation, it was decided to address the Council on the subject,
and to request that no building permit be issued to the landlords
concerned; also that police be sent to protect the tenants. The
Council is asked to grant the request in the interest of peace and
good order.
(Chopped) Shanghai First Special District
Citizens' Federation.

日期 1934年2月22日

主题（全称）减租运动

由第六区（闸北）泥水匠与木匠工会发起的反对减租运动的抗争活动，理由是若减租运动持续进行，房地产业主将停止所有现有建筑合同的工作，该活动已得到第一区（南市）、第五区（浦东）、第七区（江湾）、第八区（吴淞）和第九区（法华）泥水匠与木匠工会的加入。第二区（法租界）、第三区（公共租界）和第四区（闸北西部）的泥水匠和木匠尚未表示有意参与此次抗争。第六区工会位于闸北明立路泰德西里8号的办事处，正作为反减租运动的总部。

POLICE FORCE FOR INFORMATION
OVD 20 FEB. 1934
Translation of Petition to Council from the
Shanghai 6th District Masons and Carpenters'
Association.
Dated 13th February, 1934.

Rent reduction agitation and the building trade.

On the 6th instant a report appeared in the Press that a resolution had been passed by the Shanghai Realty Owners' Association to the effect that in view of the movement started by tenants for rent reduction, no new building operations would be taken in hand. A number of workmen belonging to this Association of Masons and Carpenters have consequently applied to us to assist them out of this difficulty. We accordingly appointed an officer to enquire into the matter and he reports that the representations made are correct.

On the 10th instant we issued a warning through the Press in which we requested the Rent Reduction Committee to consider the livelihood of over 300,000 workmen of this Association. A reply has been received from that Committee dealing with the matter in its own way and regardless of facts.

This Association finds that over 300,000 workmen have no definite work of a permanent nature. They are dependent on the occasional building of houses for their living. If work on new buildings must stop, then not only will the 300,000 workmen be deprived of occupation but the trades connected with house building will lose business. Since the workmen have been given to understand that no new building work is to be taken in hand they are in a state of unrest. It is feared that it will not be easy to pacify so many people. If no suitable measure is devised to meet the situation, these men may engage in unlawful pursuits. In the interest of the men and also of peace and order the Council is asked to restrain the Rent Reduction Committee so that the livelihood of over 300,000 men may be assured and hidden dangers removed and disturbances averted.

A petition is also being addressed to the Shanghai City Government and the French Municipal Council.

(Chopped) Shanghai 6th District Masons & Carpenters' Association.
(Signed) Tsou Zeng-yuan, Member of Standing Committee.

上海第六区泥水匠与木匠协会致工部局的请愿书译文。
日期 1934年2月13日。

减租煽动与建筑业。

本月6日，报刊刊登一则报道，称上海房地产业主协会通过一项决议，鉴于租户发起的减租运动，将不再承接新的建筑工程。本泥水匠与木匠协会的多名工人因此向我们求助，希望协助他们摆脱困境。我们随即指派一名官员调查此事，他报告称所述情况属实。

本月10日，我们通过报刊发出警告，请求减租委员会考虑本协会三十多万工人的生计。该委员会已复函，但其处理方式自行其是，不顾事实。

本协会发现，三十多万工人没有固定的长期工作。他们依靠偶尔的房屋建造工作维持生计。如果新建工程必须停止，那么不仅这三十万工人将失业，与房屋建造相关的行业也将失去业务。由于工人们已得知将不再承接新的建筑工程，他们处于不安状态。恐怕安抚如此众多的人群并非易事。若不制定适当措施应对局势，这些人可能会从事非法活动。为了工人的利益，也为了和平与秩序，恳请工部局约束减租委员会，以确保三十多万人的生计，消除隐患，避免骚乱。

另有一份请愿书正递交给上海市政府和法公董局。

（盖章）上海第六区泥水匠与木匠协会。
（签名）邹增源，常务委员。

Date February 19, 1934

Subject (in full) General meeting of the Japanese Amalgamated Association of
Street Unions held on February 17.

Made by D. S. Umemoto. Forwarded by A. J. Everson

Between 3.15 p.m. and 5.45 p.m. February 17, a general
meeting of the Japanese Amalgamated Association of Street Unions
was held at the Japanese Club, Boone Road. The function was
attended by 43 chairmen of the various street unions.
The opening speech was delivered by Mr. Amano, Vice-chairman
of the Japanese Amalgamated Association of Street Unions. Detailed
reports on the work of the Association and its financial condition
during 1933 were submitted by committee members and were approved.
In connection with the increase in the number of Japanese
members on the Shanghai Municipal Council, Mr. Hayashi, Chairman
of the Association, said that the suggestion of appointing three
Japanese members to the Shanghai Municipal Council was reasonable
and would contribute towards the maintenance of closer relations
between the Municipal Council and the Japanese community.
Mr. Takahashi, Chairman of the Showa Union, reported on
the result of a meeting held recently by a number of Japanese
residents and officials of the Shanghai Telephone Company when
the question of alleged discriminatory treatment by the Telephone
Company between subscribers in the Northern and Western Districts
was discussed.
A proposal that the question of the reduction of rentals be
studied by a committee to be appointed by the Chairman was
submitted by the Northern Branch of the Japanese Amalgamated
Association of Street Unions.
Messrs. Kanaya, Chairman of the Darroch Road Street Union,
and Takahashi, Chairman of the Showa Union, delivered a speech
supporting this proposal, which was eventually passed unanimously.
The members of the committee for the study of the high rate of
rentals and the reduction movement will be appointed later.

Subject (in full) Rent reduction movements amongst Japanese.

Made by D. S. Umemoto. Forwarded by O. J. Townsend

At 7 p.m. February 9, four committee members of the Northern District Branch of the Japanese Amalgamated Association of Street Unions held a meeting at the residence of Mr. Fukushima, No. 38 Magnolia Terrace off North Szechuen Road Extension to discuss the question of the rent reduction movement.

The meeting decided to make an investigation into the prices of commodities during the past several years, to make a comparison between the prices of commodities and the rent as well as a comparison between rent, land values and the percentage of profit of the landlords. After collecting sufficient data, the Japanese tenants in the Northern District will first obtain approval from the Japanese Amalgamated Association of Street Unions to negotiate direct with their respective landlords.

A member of the standing committee of the Japanese Amalgamated Association of Street Unions informs me that the matter has not yet been discussed by the Association.

A general meeting of the Japanese Amalgamated Association of Street Unions will be held in the Japanese Club on February 17 when it is expected that the question of the rent reduction movement will be discussed and the attitude to be adopted by Japanese in this matter will be decided. But it is generally believed that Mr. Hayashi, Chairman of the Association, will not take an active part in this movement in view of the fact that he is also a landlord.

It is learned that the landlord of a block of houses in Shing Nyih Fong (興業坊) off Scott Road, which are chiefly occupied by Japanese, has voluntarily reduced the rent from $60 to $50 per mensem, as from this month.

At present the rent reduction movement is being supported

2月9日晚7时，日本街道工会联合会北区分会的四名委员在北四川路延伸段木兰里（Magnolia Terrace）38号福岛先生（Mr. Fukushima）的寓所举行会议，讨论减租运动问题。

会议决定调查过去几年的商品价格，比较商品价格与租金，以及租金、地价与房东利润率之间的关系。在收集足够的数据后，北区的日籍租户将首先获得日本街道工会联合会的批准，然后直接与各自的房东进行谈判。

日本街道工会联合会常务委员会的一名成员告知我，该协会尚未讨论此事。

日本街道工会联合会将于2月17日在日本俱乐部举行大会，预计届时将讨论减租运动问题，并决定日侨在此事上应采取的态度。但人们普遍认为，鉴于林先生（Mr. Hayashi，协会主席）本人也是房东，他不会积极参与此次运动。

据悉，斯科特路（Scott Road）兴业坊（Shing Nyih Fong）的一排主要由日侨居住的房屋，其房东已自愿从本月起将月租金从60元降至50元。

目前，减租运动正得到支持

POLICE FORCE MUNICIPAL COUNCIL
C. & S. D. REG. 1934.
No. D J 4 8 2
Translation of letter to Secretary from
Shanghai First Special District Citizens'
Federation.
Dated 10th February, 1934.

Rent reduction and water supply.

In compliance with the numerous requests of citizens in this
city, we are now conducting a movement for the reduction of rents.
Meanwhile, malicious landlords who ignore the hardships of business-
people, are pressing for the payment and attempting to raise rentals
on the plea of increase in water charges. If their demands are not
acceded to, they will take steps to cut off the water supply immediate-
ly, and thus endanger the lives and property of tenants. When the
question was submitted to the Committee of the Citizens' Federation
for consideration, it was decided to request the Council to constant-
ly watch the landlords and to prohibit increase in rents so that
peace and good order may be preserved and the difficulties confront-
ing business establishments may be relieved.

Will the Council kindly instruct the officers concerned to deal
with this matter. The Council, being responsible for public safety,
should keep a close watch over the landlords and suppress such un-
lawful acts as the cutting off of the water supply. If the supply
of water to any house has already been discontinued, the Waterworks
Company should be directed promptly to restore it. In the interest of
Municipal administration and public safety, it is hoped that the
Secretary will give his attention to this matter.

(Chopped) Shanghai First Special District Citizens' Federation.

上海第一特区市民联合会致秘书信函的译文。
日期 1934年2月10日。

减租与供水。

应本市市民的多次请求，我们目前正在开展减租运动。与此同时，一些无视商人疾苦的恶意房东，以水费上涨为由，催缴租金并试图提高租金。如果他们的要求得不到满足，他们将立即采取措施切断供水，从而危及租户的生命和财产安全。当此问题提交给市民联合会委员会审议时，决定请求公董局持续监视房东，禁止增加租金，以便维持治安秩序，缓解商号面临的困难。

恳请公董局指示有关官员处理此事。公董局负有公共安全之责，应严密监视房东，制止切断供水等违法行为。如果任何房屋的供水已被切断，应指令自来水公司迅速恢复供水。出于市政管理和公共安全的考虑，希望秘书对此事予以关注。

（盖章）上海第一特区市民联合会。

page_data.en:
Translation of the letter addressed to the Carpenters
and masons union by the Shanghai Rent Reduction
Committee

A perusal of the warning inserted by you in
the advertisement column of the Shun Pao dated
February 10, 1934, makes us feel strange. This
Committee has the backing of public opinion and is
therefore impartial. You should, instead of
opposing this Committee, sympathize with its
activities. The reasons for this are twofold,
firstly, the members of your Union will also
benefit should the rent reduction movement prove
successful; secondly, they will have more work
than heretofore should the Estate Owners' Association
accept the proposal of the Committee to build
residences on vacant ground with a view to restoring
Shanghai to its former prosperous condition.
From the above we conclude that you have adopted a
one-sided view in sending us the warning and we
hereby earnestly offer you our advice.

上海减租委员会致木匠和泥瓦匠工会信函的译文

阅毕贵方于1934年2月10日刊登在《申报》广告栏中的警告信，令我们感到诧异。本委员会拥有舆论支持，因此是公正无私的。你们不应反对本委员会，而应同情本委员会的活动。原因有二：首先，如果减租运动取得成功，贵工会成员也将受益；其次，如果地产业主协会接受本委员会关于在空地上建造住宅以使上海恢复往日繁荣景象的建议，他们将比以往有更多的工作机会。综上所述，我们认为贵方发出警告是持片面观点，特此诚恳提出建议。

Some thirty residents of the Fan Sung Li (藩生里)
Alleyway (Lane 685), East Seward Road, held a meeting
between 5.10 p.m. and 7 p.m. February 5 in House No.3
in the alleyway. The following resolutions were discussed
and passed:-
1. That the notice of the landlords of the alleyway
to the effect that commencing from January 1, 1934
the house rent would be increased by 20% be ignored.
2. That the landlords be requested to reduce the rent
to 80% of that paid at the beginning of 1925. (The
house rent in this alleyway was increased by 20% in
the latter part of that year.)
3. That pending a settlement of the dispute, tenants be
instructed to deposit their house rent in the Shanghai
Commercial & Savings Bank.
Following an order issued in the beginning
of January, 1934, by the landlords of the Ziang Shing
Li (祥鑫里), Tatung Road near Shanhaikwan Road ordering the
tenants to vacate the premises before January 31 as the houses
would be pulled down, the residents of fifteen of the forty
five houses in the alleyway vacated their homes but the
remaining thirty tenants continue to occupy their premises
and are pressing the landlords to postpone the demolition
of the block. These residents have decided to solicit
assistance from the Shanghai Municipality Rent Reduction
Committee in connection with the dispute.

Association of the 2nd Special District Citizens' Federation

Subject (in full) Rent Reduction Movement.

Made by D.S. Mac Adie Forwarded by W. Duncan DS

As a measure to further the rent reduction movement
the Shanghai Municipality Rent Reduction Committee organized
by various local public bodies with an office in the Chinese
Chamber of Commerce building, North Soochow Road, has decided
to divide Shanghai into five districts, International Settlement,
French Concession, Chapei, Nantao and Pootung, each with a
"District Association" to deal with disputes arising out of
the rent reduction movement in their respective areas.
The District Associations of the first three areas above
mentioned were formally inaugurated in January, 1934, while
efforts are being made for the formation of the Associations
in the remaining two Districts, Nantao and Pootung. The
Committee in addition has instructed the Branch Associations
of the 1st and 2nd Special District Citizens' Federations
to act as "Rent Reduction Movement Sub-Offices" to assist
the District Associations in the Settlement and French Concession
in supervising the activities of section offices organized
by the residents in various alleyways. Up to the present
a total of five section offices as shown in the following
table have been formed by tenants of various alleyways in
the Settlements:-

The Rent Reduction Movement Committee has prepared
a handbill entitled "A Manifesto issued in connection with
the Rent Reduction Movement" which was distributed to its
branches on January 3. The document states that as a result
of the Sino-Japanese Hostilities in 1932 for which the
Japanese are to be blamed, local business is greatly depressed.
In the programme of rehabilitation of Shanghai and restoration
to its former prosperous condition are a number of necessary
measures but the principal and the most pressing of these
is the movement for the reduction in house rentals. This
reduction will relieve the residents from their present
straitened circumstances.

February 6, 34.

Rent Reduction Movement.

Del. Mac Aule

As a measure to further the rent reduction movement
the Shanghai Municipality Rent Reduction Committee organized
by various local public bodies with an office in the Chinese
Chamber of Commerce building, North Soochow Road, has decided
to divide Shanghai into five districts, International Settlement,
French Concession, Chapei, Nantao and Pootung, each with a
"District Association" to deal with disputes arising out of
the rent reduction movement in their respective areas.
The District Associations of the first three areas above
mentioned were formally inaugurated in January, 1934, while
efforts are being made for the formation of the Associations
in the remaining two Districts, Nantao and Pootung. The
Committee in addition has instructed the branch associations
of the 1st and 2nd Special District Citizens' Federations
to act as "Rent Reduction Movement Sub-Offices" to assist
the District Associations in the Settlement and French Concession
in supervising the activities of section offices organized
by the residents in various alleyways. Up to the present
a total of five section offices as shown in the following
table have been formed by tenants of various alleyways in
the Settlement:-

减租运动。

作为推进减租运动的一项措施，由各地公共团体组织、办事处设于北苏州路中国商会大楼内的上海市减租委员会决定，将上海划分为五个区：公共租界、法租界、闸北、南市和浦东，各区设立一个“区协会”，以处理各自区域内因减租运动而产生的纠纷。上述前三个区的区协会已于1934年1月正式成立，而其余两个区（南市和浦东）的协会正在努力组建中。此外，该委员会还指示第一和第二特区市民联合会的分会充当“减租运动分办事处”，协助公共租界和法租界的区协会，监督由各里弄居民组织的分段办事处的活动。截至目前，公共租界内各里弄租户已成立了如下表所示的共五个分段办事处：

The Rent Reduction Movement Committee has prepared
a handbill entitled "A Manifesto issued in connection with
the Rent Reduction Movement" which was distributed to its
branches on January 3. The document states that as a result
of the Sino-Japanese Hostilities in 1932 for which the
Japanese are to be blamed, local business is greatly depressed.
In the programme of rehabilitation of Shanghai and restoration
to its former prosperous condition are a number of necessary
measures but the principal and the most pressing of these
is the movement for the reduction in house rentals. This
reduction will relieve the residents from their present
straitened circumstances.

January 29, 1934.

Commissioner of Police.
Sir,
Re attached report from West Hongkew.
On learning on the forenoon of January 28 that
the so-called Shanghai Municipality Rent Reduction
Committee proposed holding a motor car procession at
2 p.m. that day, I called Chang Ih-zung (张一),
a leading member of the Committee, to Headquarters and
pointed out that no sanction had been sought from the
S.M.C. He expressed regret and asked if this could be
overlooked, adding that all arrangements had been made
and giving an assurance that the so-called procession
would be limited to two vehicles only. After communicating
with D. C. (DIV), I informed Chang that the function could
go on provided only two vehicles took part and that the
route scheduled (attached) would be strictly adhered to.
To these stipulations Chang readily agreed.

At about 2 p.m. Inspector Pike, West Hongkew,
telephoned me to say that a procession of six vehicles
were about to start off from the Chamber of Commerce and
that he had informed D.C. "C" who requested I should be
notified. I instructed Inspector Pike to point out to the
responsible member of the Committee present that any
number of vehicles in excess of two was contrary to the
arrangement made with Mr. Chang and was a decided breach
of faith. This was done, but nevertheless six cars took
part and the procession did not abide by the route agreed
upon.

A show of force on the part of West Hongkew might
have had the desired result of making these people limit
the vehicles to two, but on the other hand this breach

THE HOUSE RENT REDUCTION MOVEMENT

With a view to alleviating the burdens of the
people during the present period of depression, a house
rent reduction movement committee was proposed by the
various public organizations.
On 16th January, a meeting of representatives of
the public organizations was convened at the premises of
the Chinese Chamber of Commerce, North Soochow Road, at
which the regulations governing the organization of the
committee were passed and 35 persons were elected members
of the Committee.
It is ascertained that the first meeting of the
Committee will take place at 2 p.m. to-morrow at the Chinese
Chamber of Commerce and a notification has been issued
to the members.

Following the launching of a house rent reduction
movement by the various Chinese public organizations, many
foreign residents associations have decided to call a meeting
in a few days for the purpose of discussing the advisability
of joining the movement.
According to the opinions of foreign residents,
not only should the house rent be reduced, but charges for
electricity, gas, water and telephone service should also
be lowered, for they consider that the prevailing depression
has affected not only Chinese residents but the foreigners
as well. They contend that prices have dropped everywhere
in the world except in Shanghai, where the house rent and
rates for all public utilities have increased.
The reduction movement is being sponsored chiefly
by the Japanese Streets Federation, the White Russian
Merchants Federation, the Indian Federation, the Portuguese
Residents Association and other residents and trade asso-
ciations. Even a number of British residents are supporting
the movement.
In Shanghai, there are about 50,000 foreigners.
The total amount of house-rent paid by them is nearly equal
to the amount paid by Chinese tenants (in the International
Settlement the Chinese pay about $3,000,000 while the
foreigners about $2,600,000), whereas the amounts of charges
paid by foreigners for electricity, water and gas are more
than those paid by Chinese.
The Shanghai Municipal Council has a voice in the
control of these undertakings, but the actual power is held
by the principals directors of these companies. Inasmuch as

减租运动

为减轻当前萧条时期民众的负担，各公共团体提议成立一个减租运动委员会。
1月16日，各公共团体代表会议在北苏州路中国商会会所召开，会上通过了委员会组织章程，并选举35人为委员会委员。
据悉，委员会第一次会议将于明日下午2时在中国商会举行，通知已发给各位委员。

继中国各公共团体发起减租运动后，许多外侨协会决定在数日内召开会议，讨论加入该运动是否适宜。
据外侨意见，不仅房租应当降低，电费、煤气费、水费和电话服务费也应下调，因为他们认为目前的萧条不仅影响了中国居民，也影响了外国人。他们主张，世界各地物价均已下跌，唯独上海例外，那里的房租和所有公用事业费率反而上涨。
此次减租运动主要由日本街道联合会、白俄商人联合会、印度人联合会、葡萄牙居民协会以及其他居民和贸易协会发起。甚至一些英国居民也支持该运动。
在上海，外侨约有5万人。他们支付的房租总额几乎与中国租户支付的金额相等（在公共租界，中国人支付约300万元，而外国人支付约260万元），而外国人支付的电、水、煤气费用则高于中国人。

landlords to suspend collection of rents in the zone directly

These regulations aroused considerable agitation among persons
connected with rent reduction movements as they considered that
the landlords were being favoured and also as no mention had
been made of a remission of rents of houses situated in the
Pootung and other areas. In addition to an appeal for the
rescission of the proclamation the discharge and punishment of
Mr. O. K. Yu, Secretary of the Municipality of Greater Shanghai,
was also called for as he was considered to have been responsible
for the drafting of the regulations.
Numerous meetings were subsequently held at
which the usual resolutions of refusal to pay rent, demands
for a reduction of rent, etc. were passed but nothing definite
occurred until two of the realty companies sued their tenants
in the Shanghai Special District Court for arrears of rent.
These companies were the Metropolitan Land Company and the
Cathay Land Company and in both cases decisions were handed
down in their favour. The decisions were made public in
July, 1932 and from that time little or no agitation has been

随着大上海市长发布关于免租和减租的公告，市民联合会及其他团体举行会议，表达了对该公告所定条款的不满。看来大部分不满情绪源于苏州河以南地区未获得任何救济，而据称居住在这些地区的居民在中日敌对行动期间被迫停业，遭受了重大损失。在7月21日于华商总会举行的市民联合会会议上，决定派遣五名委员前往南京，就吴市长于7月9日发布的公告条款不公一事向政府交涉。大上海市政府已阻止了这一行动，并在7月23日的《申报》上发布公告，告知公众市长的公告条款已由南京行政院颁布。

Citizens' Federation - meeting

17 members of the Citizens' Federation held a meeting
in the Chinese Chamber of Commerce Building, North Honan Road,
between 4 and 6 p.m. July 21 and passed the following
resolutions:-

1. That a Rent Reduction and Exemption Committee be
organized.

2. That five representatives be sent to proceed to Nanking
and appeal to the Nanking Government in connection with
the measures relating to rent reduction and exemption
recently promulgated by the Shanghai Municipality.

3. That a general meeting be convened after the return
of these representatives.

4. That posters in connection with the movement be prepared
for posting.

5. That the following committees be organized to undertake
various tasks:

Finance Committee.
Scheme Planning Committee.
National Goods Promotion Committee.

6. That the National Government be requested to accelerate
the restoration of the lost territory in the North East.

Extract from the Intelligence Report dated 21/7/32

Citizens Federation and dissatisfaction with rent
measures of Shanghai Municipality

Strong dissatisfaction now exists among the
members of the Citizens Federation and the Rent
Reduction and Exemption Movement Committee with
Mr. Yui Hung-chung, Secretary of the Shanghai
Municipality who, it is alleged, is responsible for
the drafting of regulations governing rent reduction
and exemption recently promulgated by the Shanghai
Municipality. These measures have since the
announcement met with strong opposition from these
associations on the ground that the residents in the
area to the south of the Soochow Creek do not benefit
by them. It is reported that in the event of
the Shanghai Municipality continuing to ignore the
opposition and refusing to make any amendments, these
associations will send representatives to Nanking
and appeal to the Nanking Government.

市民联合会及对上海市政府租金措施的不满

市民联合会成员及减租免租运动委员会成员对上海市政府秘书长余鸿钟（Yui Hung-chung，音译）存在强烈不满，据称他负责起草了上海市政府最近颁布的减租免租规定。自宣布以来，这些措施遭到了这些协会的强烈反对，理由是苏州河以南地区的居民未能从中受益。据报道，如果上海市政府继续无视反对意见并拒绝做任何修改，这些协会将派遣代表前往南京，向南京政府提出申诉。

Citizens' Federation - Meeting

Some 50 representatives of various branches of the
Citizens' Federation held a meeting in the Chamber of
Commerce, North Honan Road, between 3 and 7 p.m. July 15,
when the following resolutions were discussed and passed:

1. That the following measures be adopted against the
proclamation of the Greater Shanghai Municipality on
rent reduction (which does not satisfy the expectations
of the Federation) :-

a) That a manifesto opposing the proclamation be issued.

b) That the Municipality of Greater Shanghai be told
of the improper as well as omitted points in the
proclamation and be requested to withdraw it and
to promulgate another complete one.

c) That an appeal be made to the National Government.

d) That a general strike of local shops be resorted to
when necessary to enforce the demand.

e) That a "Rent Reduction and Remission Special
Committee" be organized.

f) That the local Kuomintang be informed of the
improper as well as omitted points in connection
with rent remission in the proclamation issued by
the Municipality.

g) That the local judicial authorities be requested to
be lenient to the tenants in rent cases.

h) That the Chinese Ratepayers' Association be requested
to ask the S.M.C. and not to interfere in rent
disputes on behalf of landlords until the rent
remission dispute is settled by the Federation with
the Municipality.

i) That the National Government be requested to dismiss
forthwith the Chief Secretary of the Municipality
(Yu Hung-chun) and adequately punish him for offering
wrong opinions on rent reduction and remission.

2. That the Special Committee To Oppose the Increase in
Telephone Charges be instructed to negotiate with the
S.M.C. and the Company for the cancellation of the
increase, and local subscribers be told to pay the
charges according to the old scale.

3. That opposition be made to the signing of a "Loss of
Right" agreement in connection with the local extra
Settlement roads.

7月15日下午3时至7时，市民联合会各分会的约50名代表在华商总会举行会议，讨论并通过了以下决议：

1. 针对大上海市政府关于减租的公告（该公告未能满足联合会的期望），采取以下措施：-

a) 发布反对该公告的宣言。

b) 告知大上海市政府公告中的不当之处及遗漏点，并要求其撤回公告，重新颁布一份完整的公告。

c) 向国民政府提出申诉。

d) 必要时采取本地商店总罢工的手段来强制执行要求。

e) 组织“减租免租特别委员会”。

f) 将市政府发布的公告中关于免租的不当之处及遗漏点告知当地国民党。

g) 请求当地司法机关在租金案件中从宽对待租户。

h) 请求华人纳税会要求工部局不要代表房东干预租金纠纷，直到联合会与市政府解决免租争议为止。

i) 请求国民政府立即罢免市政府秘书长（余鸿钧），并就其在减租免租问题上提供错误意见予以适当惩处。

2. 指示反对增加电话费特别委员会与工部局及公司谈判，取消加价，并告知本地用户按旧标准缴费。

Made by....D. S. Golder................Forwarded by Thos Robertson, Supt

in connection with the proclamation regarding rent
reduction and remission issued by the Municipality of Greater
Shanghai on Saturday, July 9, a visit was paid to the office
of Mr. A.M. Preston, (No.43 Peking Road,) Vice-Chairman of the
Shanghai Property Owners' Association." He stated when
approached regarding the proclamation that the terms laid
down therein were very much the same as those agreed upon
by the association of which he is the Vice Chairman and
that so far as he could at present see there would be nothing
to gain by making any protest in the matter. In most cases
the remission and reduction of rent conforms with the scheme
for the remission of the Municipal Rate, whilst the proclamation
issued by the Municipality does not differ materially from
the rate remission scheme.

Between 4.45 and 6.35 p.m. on July 10 at a meeting
in their offices on Chefoo Road the Rent Reduction and
Remission Committee discussed and passed the following
resolutions:

1. That a petition to be submitted to the Municipality be
drafted pointing out the unfairness of the measures dealing
with rent reduction and remission promulgated by the
Municipality.

2. That tenants of Shanghai be notified pending a satisfactory
reply from the Shanghai Municipality to the above petition
to withhold rent payment.

3. That the Central Government be requested to instruct the
Shanghai Municipality to reconsider the matter.

4. That a circular telegram be despatched soliciting assistance
from the nation concerning the matter.

主题（全称）........租金减免与减租

制作人....D. S. Golder................呈送人 Thos Robertson，警司

鉴于大上海市政府于7月9日（星期六）发布了关于减租和免租的公告，本人走访了上海业主协会副主席A.M. Preston先生（北京路43号）的办公室。他就该公告表示，其中规定的条款与他所任副主席的协会所商定的条款大致相同，就他目前所见，对此事提出任何抗议并无益处。在大多数情况下，租金的减免符合市政捐税减免方案，而市政府发布的公告与捐税减免方案并无实质性差异。

7月10日下午4时45分至6时35分，租金减免委员会在其芝罘路办公室举行的会议上讨论并通过了以下决议：

1. 起草一份提交给市政府的请愿书，指出市政府颁布的关于减租和免租的措施存在不公。

2. 在上海市政府对上述请愿书作出令人满意的答复之前，通知上海租户暂停支付租金。

3. 请求中央政府指令上海市政府重新审议此事。

4. 发出通函电报，就此事项向全国寻求援助。

Subject (in full) Rent Remission and Reduction

Made by D. S. Golder Forwarded by Thos Robertson, Supt

The tenants of the Shanghai Land Investment Company's
estate on East Kashing Road, Mukden Road, Thorne Road and
Urga Road who on June 25 began agitation for the reduction
of rent have ceased such agitation since the landlords have
promised to remit rent for the whole of April. In this
connection a visit was paid to the offices of the Shanghai
Land Investment Company, 32 Jinkee Road on July 7th when Mr.
Buck informed the undersigned that so far as he could see the

Subject (in full) Shanghai Citizens Rent Reduction and Remission
Movement Committee - General Meeting.

Made by D. S. Golder Forwarded by Jhd Robertson, Supt.

One hundred and thirty two Chinese claiming to
represent various local bodies attended a meeting convened
by the Shanghai Citizens Rent Reduction and Remission Movement
Committee in the Zang Kung Primary School, 186 Burkill
Road, at 3 p.m. June 26 and passed the following resolutions:
1. That the Shanghai Municipality be requested to promulgate
before the end of June measures for dealing with rent
reduction and remission.
2. That the Shanghai Municipality be requested to request
the Judicial Authorities not to hear any case regarding
the current rent dispute until these measures have been
promulgated.
3. That seven representatives be appointed to submit an
appeal to the Shanghai Municipality regarding the rent
question.
4. That local various bodies be instructed to submit
similar appeals to the Municipality.
5. That a manifesto be issued advocating the necessity
for rent reduction and exemption.
6. That those tenants who have entered into agreement
with the landlords regarding rent reduction be entitled
to the same reduction and exemption as those who so far
have not done so.
7. That the local water companies be requested to continue
the supply of water to tenants irrespective of the
application of the landlords for discontinuance of supply
as a counter measure against the non-payment of rent.
8. That pending the promulgation of measures by the
Municipality, the rentals be deposited in the banks.

制作人 D. S. Golder 呈送人 Jhd Robertson，警司。

一百三十二名自称代表各地方团体的华人出席了由上海市民减租免租运动委员会于6月26日下午3时在伯基尔路186号藏公小学召开的会议，并通过了以下决议：
1. 请求上海市政府在六月底前颁布处理减租和免租的措施。
2. 请求上海市政府要求司法当局在这些措施颁布之前，不予受理任何有关当前租金纠纷的案件。
3. 指派七名代表就租金问题向上海市政府提交上诉。
4. 指示各地方团体向市政府提交类似的上诉。
5. 发布宣言，倡导减租和免税的必要性。
6. 凡已与房东就减租达成协议的租户，应享有与尚未达成协议的租户相同的减免待遇。
7. 请求本地自来水公司继续向租户供水，不论房东是否以停水作为对抗拒付租金的反制措施而申请停止供水。
8. 在市政府颁布措施之前，将租金存入银行。

Subject (in full) Rent Remission and Reduction.

Made by D. S. Golder Forwarded by Jhn Robertson, Supt.

At 10.30 a.m. June 25 a visit was paid to the Shanghai Land Investment Company, No.32 Jinkee Road, when Mr. Buck handed to the undersigned three documents in Chinese(attached hereto) which were distributed to the tenants of the Shanghai Land Investment Company' property on East Kashing, Thorne, Mukden, Dixwell and Urga Roads. Two were handbills purporting to have been issued by the Propaganda Department of the Shanghai Zuan Ching, Zuan Kong and Zuan Yui, Three Alleyways Tenants Union, office No.3, Lane No.304 East Kashing Road, which read as follows:
Poster 1 We shall not pay the rent until the object of rent reduction and remission is attained!
Poster 2 The only method of lengthy resistance is to deposit the rentals in banks.
The third was a card issued by the National Industrial Bank of China and bearing the chop in red and purple of the above Union. The Union are urging the tenants to pay their rent into the above mentioned bank (Hongkew Branch) and not to withdraw it or pay the landlords who are the Shanghai Land Investment Company unless ordered to do so by the Union.
The Shanghai Land Investment Company granted the tenants in the areas mentioned above two months remission of rent; later, however, the Council granted three months remission of Municipal Rates, the Company therefore considered the granting of a further month but so far has not done so. The action on the part of the Union in causing the tenants to pay their rent into the bank is considered by the Company as highly irregular and liable in the future to cause a great deal of dissatisfaction among the people concerned.

制作人 D. S. Golder 呈送人 Jhn Robertson，警司。

6月25日上午10时30分，本人走访了位于江西路32号的上海置业公司，Buck先生向本人递交了三份中文文件（附后），这些文件已分发给上海置业公司位于嘉兴东路、Thorne路（音译）、沈阳路、Dixwell路（音译）和乌尔加路（音译）的物业租户。其中两份是传单，声称由上海钻精、钻公和钻玉（音译）三弄租户联合会宣传部发布，办公地址为嘉兴东路304弄3号，内容如下：
海报1 在实现减租免租目标之前，我们将不支付租金！
海报2 长期抵抗的唯一方法是将租金存入银行。
第三份是由中国国货银行发行的卡片，上面盖有上述联合会的红紫色印章。该联合会敦促租户将租金存入上述银行（虹口分行），除非得到联合会的命令，否则不得提取或支付给作为房东的上海置业公司。

上海置业公司曾给予上述地区租户两个月的租金减免；然而，后来工部局给予了三个月的市政捐税减免，因此公司考虑再给予一个月的减免，但截至目前尚未实施。公司认为，联合会促使租户将租金存入银行的行为极不规范，将来很可能在相关人群中引起大量不满。

（左侧手写批注：Jly m/l）

Members of the Chinese Realty Owners' Association
numbering at present 120, held a meeting at 3.30 p.m.

National Commercial Bank Ltd, Realty Trust Department, 74
Szechuen Road, Chairman of the Association presided, and
the following resolutions were passed :
1. That the S.M.C. be requested to give an explanation for
having approved without first consulting with the consumers
the decision of the Shanghai Water Works to collect the
water rate according to meter reading, and that the
Council be apprised of the disregard of the Company for
the position of the estate owners by resolving to cut
off water supply for non-payment. The adoption of

people.

Creek be reduced or remitted in proportion as the ratio
devised by the Municipal Council regarding reduction and
remission of the Municipal Rates and that the Shanghai
Water Works, Shanghai Power Company and the Municipal
Council be respectively asked to remit the water rate,
electricity charges and land tax during the period when
rentals are remitted.
3. That all members refuse to sign contract for water supply
according to meter system.
4. That estate owners be advised to construct artesian wells
for water supply.
5. That the Shanghai Water Works be advised to adopt the

Made by D.S. Tilton Forwarded by Tho Robertson, Supt.

The North Chang Kang Li Tenants Association was
inaugurated on April 10, 1932 with an office at No.207 North
Chang Kang Li, Alabaster Road. The Committee consisted of
Chang Tung Sung (張東生), tenant of No.198, and Hsu
Chih-an (許志安), tenant of No.206 and Mi Peng-tah
(米本德), tenant at No.176 of the afore-mentioned
alleyway. The membership numbered 56 tenants who each
subscribed 50 cents which was expended by the Committee as
expenses. Negotiations were immediately commenced between
the estate agents D.H. Benjamin and Co., 259 Kiangse Road
and the association who requested 3 months remission of rents
and arrears of rents to be paid by instalments, while the
estate agents desired the arrears to be immediately settled and
they would allow 2 months remission.

The Committee members stated that they represented
bona-fide tenants only of the houses of the above estate
agent situated in that locality, and rather than prolong the
matter to an indefinite period and to avoid any action in the
Shanghai Special District Court, the Association intended
later to propose to the estate agents a 2 months' rent
remission and arrears settled by instalments, as the tenants
had undoubtedly suffered considerable hardships from loss of
employment and forced to rent other premises in safe zones,
and thus immediate settlement of arrears of rent is impossible.

The Committee members stated they did not desire to
gain any unjust profit from their labour, their work was
purely representing the tenants and not prompted by any ulterior
motives, they had no wish to amalgamate with other associations
formed for the purpose of rent reduction and remission. Their

北长康里房客联合会于1932年4月10日成立，办事处设在阿拉白司脱路北长康里207号。委员会由该弄堂198号租户张东生（Chang Tung Sung）、206号租户许志安（Hsu Chih-an）和176号租户米本德（Mi Peng-tah）组成。会员共有56名租户，每人缴纳50美分，由委员会作为经费支出。随即在地产代理人江西路259号 D.H. Benjamin 公司与该协会之间展开谈判，协会要求免租3个月并分期支付欠租，而地产代理人希望立即结清欠租，并同意免租2个月。

委员会成员表示，他们仅代表该地区上述地产代理人所属房屋的正牌租户，为了避免将此事无限期拖延并避免在上海特区法院采取任何行动，协会打算随后向地产代理人提出免租2个月并分期结算欠租的建议，因为租户无疑因失业遭受了巨大困难，并被迫在安全区租赁其他住所，因此立即结清欠租是不可能的。

Subject (in full) Shanghai Citizens' Rent Reduction and Exemption Movement
Committee - Promoters, aims and objects

Made by D. I. Sih Tsz-liang Forwarded by Tho Robertson Supt

The Shanghai Citizens' Rent Reduction and Exemption
Movement Committee 上海市民減免房租運動委員會 with offices at
251 Chefoo Road was inaugurated at a meeting held in the
Ground Nut Dealers Association, 101 Chihli Road on March 19,
1932 by representatives of various public bodies (Vide attached/ extract from the
Intelligence Report of March 21, 1932). The principal
promoters of this body are :
Chu Wei Sung (褚慧僧 ), Chairman of the Chekiang Provincials'
Association, (Lien Chi Li, Avenue Road) and a committee
member of the National Salvation Association of Various
Shanghai Bodies (91 Bubbling Well Terrace, Bubbling Well
Road),
Yui Hwa Loong (余華龍 ), committee member of the Citizens'
Federation (Chinese Chamber of Commerce Building, North
Honan Road) and a lawyer, 21 Burkill Road, and
Yuan Hung Chiung (袁鴻鈞 ), representative of the Shoe Model
Shop Owners' Association, formerly at Chapei. Important
officer in the Propaganda Department of the defunct National
Salvation Committee to Resist Japan. Privately, he acted as
liaison officer between the Committee and the "traitorous"
merchants.

The Committee is an organization formed for the
purpose of persuading the landlords to suspend the collection
of rent or reduce the rentals for premises in the Settlement.
This being so, it is not in position to force either land-
lords or tenants to comply with its proposals. In the event
of a landlord insisting upon collecting the full amount of
rent due, the Committee has no redress but will resort to
petitioning the Courts should civil action be commenced

主题（全称）上海市民减免房租运动委员会——发起人、宗旨及目标

由侦探督察 Sih Tsz-liang 制作，经警司 Tho Robertson 转呈

上海市民减免房租运动委员会（Shanghai Citizens' Rent Reduction and Exemption Movement Committee），办公地点位于芝罘路251号，于1932年3月19日在直隶路101号的花生业公会举行的会议上，由各公共团体代表宣布成立（参见附后的1932年3月21日情报报告摘录）。该组织的主要发起人为：
褚慧僧（Chu Wei Sung），浙江省同乡会主席（连嘉里，爱文义路），也是上海各团体救国会（静安寺路91号，静安寺路）的委员，
余華龍（Yui Hwa Loong），市民联合会（河南北路商会大楼）委员及律师，办公地址为伯克路21号，以及
袁鴻鈞（Yuan Hung Chiung），鞋模店业主协会代表，原籍闸北。前抗日救国委员会宣传部重要官员。私下里，他担任该委员会与“奸商”之间的联络官。

该委员会是一个旨在说服房东暂停收取或降低租界内房屋租金而成立的组织。鉴于此，它无权强迫房东或租户遵守其提议。如果房东坚持收取全额到期租金，委员会除了诉诸法律外别无补救办法；一旦对租户提起民事诉讼，委员会将向法院请愿，请求法院考虑上海公众的经济困境，并作出有利于租户的裁决。委员会已向上海各中国法院寄送了此类信函。

Subject (in full) Shanghai District Rent Reduction and Remission Movement

Made by D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by Chas Robertson, Supt.

Some 160 Chinese claiming to represent various
street unions, branches of the Citizens' Federation and
Tenants' Union held a meeting under the auspices of the
Shanghai District Rent Reduction & Remission Movement
80 Thibet Road,
Committee in the Ningpo Fellow Countrymen's Assn., / between
3 and 5.45 p.m. April 28. Yui Hwa-loong (余華龍), a
lawyer with an office at 2 Burkill Road, presided. The
following resolutions were discussed and passed:-
1. That the rents of houses in areas north of the Soochow
Creek be remitted for February, March and April, while
the rent question for May and subsequent matters be
decided in accordance with the circumstances obtaining
2. That the rents of houses in Nantao, Footung and Western
District extra-Settlement road areas be remitted for
February and March and that only 40% of the rent be
paid from April until such time as normal conditions
are restored.
3. That the rents of houses in that part of the Settlement
south of the Soochow Creek and in French Concession be
exempted from payment for February and March and that
only 50% of the rent be paid from April until such time
as normal conditions are restored.
4. That the rents of houses in Chapei, Chenju, Kiangwan,
Woosung and the areas North of the Boundary Gates of
the Settlement be totally remitted until such time
as normal conditions is restored.
5. That the 1st tenants and the sub-tenants be entitled
to equal remission and/or reduction in rent; but the
latter should pay the electricity and water rates to the

主题（全称）上海区减免房租运动委员会——会议情况

由侦探督察 Sih Tse-liang 制作，经警司 Chas Robertson 转呈。

约160名声称代表各马路商界联合会、市民联合会分会及租户联合会的华人，于4月28日下午3时至5时45分之间，在上海区减免房租运动委员会（通讯地址：西藏路80号）的主持下，在宁波同乡会举行会议。余華龍（Yui Hwa-loong），律师，办公地址为伯克路2号，担任会议主席。讨论并通过了以下决议：-
1. 苏州河以北地区的房屋租金免除二月、三月和四月的租金，五月及以后的租金问题视当时情况而定。
2. 南市、浦东及越界筑路西区地区的房屋租金免除二月和三月的租金，从四月起直至恢复正常状况为止，仅支付40%的租金。
3. 租界内苏州河以南地区及法租界的房屋租金免除二月和三月的租金，从四月起直至恢复正常状况为止，仅支付50%的租金。
4. 闸北、真如、江湾、吴淞及租界边界门以北地区的房屋租金全部免除，直至恢复正常状况为止。
5. 正租户与转租户享有同等的租金免除和/或减免权利；但后者应按比例向前者支付水电费。

Date April 29th 1932.
Subject (in full) Meeting of the General Committee for 1932 of
the Shanghai Property Owners' Association.
Made by D. S. Tilton Forwarded by Thos Robertson, Supt.

At 5 p.m. April 28, 1932, the General Committee
for 1932 of the Shanghai Property Owners' Association
held a meeting at No.28 Jinkee Road, offices of the
Shanghai Land Investment Company, Ltd. Fifteen members
attended and Mr. A.M. Preston, solicitor of Ellis and
Hays, legal practitioners, 43 Peking Road, Vice-Chairman
of the General Committee, presided. As a result of this
meeting, it was decided by the Committee to uphold and
abide with the decision of Algar & Company, Estate Agents,
No.5 Hongkong Road, acting for the Cathay Land Estate
Company in connection with a block of buildings comprising,
a hotel, a bath house, shops and houses situated at the
rear of the Wing On Company, Nanking Road, to commence
proceedings against some 25 Chinese tenants for non-payment
of rents. Formerly these tenants raised an objection to
paying the full rentals and were warned by Algar & Company
that action would be taken against them in the Shanghai
Special District Court, the tenants then agreed to pay, but
on April 26, the tenants communicated with Algar & Company,
stating they had no intention of paying the full rent and
would fight the case in the Court. The members of the
Shanghai Property Owners' Committee regard this as a test
case and will await the outcome pending further action
against their tenants. Algar & Company are at present
the only agents, who have experienced serious opposition
with tenants south of the Soochow Creek; no other complaints
have been made by the other members of the General Committee.
Mr. A.M. Preston also brought to the notice
of the members and handed in-to the meeting two letters

Translation of a Circular Letter From Shanghai
Bar Association to Its Members

Dear Sir,

We have received a letter from the Committee of Rent
Reduction and Exemption Society of French Concession, which
says :

"In accordance with the tendency of the times to
alleviate the sufferings of the populace and lessen the
burden of the people and to readjust the economic interest
of society and with a view to consolidate the unity of the
tenants that just treatment may be achieved, our Society
was organized on the 31st of March by representatives of
the different Merchants' and Tenants' Societies already
in existence. By virtue of a resolution passed by a
general meeting and by the constituted rules of this
Association, all matters relating to landlords and tenants
and to legal matters connected therewith shall be referred
to our Honorary Legal Department. Messrs. Lee Ming,
Chang Ping Chu, Liu Yung Sun, King Yu, Chen Zai Ling,
and Chow Yi Tao, all Attorneys-at-law, have been attached
to the Legal Department as Honorary Legal Advisers. As
the scope of the rent diminution movement is very wide and
the raising of legal questions are inevitable, our
Association cordially welcomes those who will join our
Legal Department as legal advisers availing us of their
learning with a view to ensure more protection. Your
Association, we understand, is a society of legal
practitioners sympathizing with the public interests.
All introduced and putting public duty before themselves
will be heartily welcomed, wherefore we write you to
ask you to circularize your members to this effect."

The above letter was laid before the 104th joint meeting
of the Executive and Supervisory Committees for discussion and
it was decided that the members should in turn be notified of

Translation of a Circular Letter from Shanghai
Bar Association to Its Members

Dear Sir,

The Association has received a letter from the
Committee of the Shanghai Residents Rent Diminution and
Exemption Movement Society which says:

"Two months have elapsed since the Japanese
agression in Shanghai. As a result of the warfare,
all businesses have declined to such a degree that
even with great decrease of expenditure on necessaries
such as clothing and food, the people nevertheless find
great difficulty in maintaining their living. It is an
obvious fact that people are financially disabled and
unable to bear the burden of rent. Our Society is an
organization set up by seventy bodies with the chief
purpose of promoting the rent diminution movement as it
is our belief that without this it is impossible to
restore local prosperity and stability to save the
people from ruin. However we are under the apprehension
that the security of residents will be greatly endangered
in the case that the landlords do not sympathize with us
and insist upon exercising their rights of property by
instituting actions in the Courts. The Society there-
fore passed a resolution that your Association should be
requested by formal letter to ask your members to refuse
to represent landlords in cases where they presume to

尊敬的先生：

本会收到上海市民减租免税运动委员会的来信，内容如下：

“上海战事爆发已两月。受战争影响，百业萧条，即便大幅缩减衣食等必需品开支，民众仍难以维持生计。民众财力枯竭、无力承担租金负担，乃显而易见之事实。本会是由七十个团体组成的组织，主要宗旨是推动减租运动，因为我们相信，若不如此，便无法恢复地方的繁荣与稳定，使民众免于破产。然而，我们担心，若房东不同情我们的处境，坚持行使财产权利并在法院提起诉讼，居民的安全将受到极大威胁。因此，本会通过决议，正式致函贵会，请求贵会要求会员在减租问题解决之前，拒绝代理房东追讨欠租的案件。鉴于贵会长期以来关心民众福祉，仁义为先，我们的请求定能得到贵会的赞同。”

Translation of petition to Council from the
Union of Tenants of Alabaster Road, North
Thibet Road, Kangsu Road, Kaifeng Road and
Jehol Road.
Dated 23rd April, 1932.
Address: 206 North Zang K'ong Li,
Alabaster Road.
(北 長 康 里).

House Rent: Reductions.

This Union is located in the northern district, - north of the
Soochow Creek and west of Kansu Road. On 28th January fighting
broke out in Shanghai and Alabaster Road became a scene of defence
activities. The situation was tense. After the erection of barbed
wire barricades on all sides, communication was cut off, and the
tenants, becoming alarmed, nearly all fled. In removing elsewhere
they suffered heavy losses. Although they have now survived the
calamity and have recovered from a state of unrest, they are still
in serious straits because their financial resources are exhausted
and they now find it difficult to earn their living. In view of this,
the various organizations in Shanghai have formed a Committee to
advocate reduction of rent, which became an urgent consideration as
a result of the fighting. Landlords, whose consciences are not dull-
ed should of their own accord reduce and remit rent in sympathy for
their tenants, who after all are as near to them "as the lips are to
the teeth". At present landlords not only evince no sympathy but
persist in demanding payment as before. The Union of "Tenants of the
Five Roads" has been organized to take proper steps in the interest
of tenants. The Council is asked to take note of the facts leading to
the organization of this Union.

(Chopped) Union of Tenants of Five Roads,
Vis:- Alabaster Road, North Thibet Road,
Kansu Road, Kaifeng Road and Jehol Road.

27/4.

C. Hsiung.
26 APR. 1932

日期：1932年4月23日。
地址：阿尔巴斯特路北张公里206号
(北長康里)。

房租：减免。

本联合会位于北区，即苏州河以北、康苏路以西。1月28日上海爆发战事，阿尔巴斯特路成为防御活动之地。局势紧张。在四周设立铁丝网路障后，交通断绝，租户惊慌，几乎全部逃离。在迁往他处时，他们遭受了重大损失。虽然他们现已度过灾难并从动荡状态中恢复，但由于财力耗尽，目前仍处境艰难，难以维持生计。鉴于此，上海各组织成立了倡导减租的委员会，这是战事导致的紧迫考量。良心未泯的房东应出于对租户的同情，主动减免租金，毕竟租户与他们“唇齿相依”。目前，房东不仅没有表现出同情，反而坚持照常催缴租金。“五路租户联合会”已组织起来，以采取适当措施维护租户利益。请工部局注意导致本联合会成立的事实。

Subject (in full) Provisional Joint Office of the Hongkew District
Branch of Citizens' Association

Made by D.S. Tilton Forwarded by Thos Robertson, Supt.

The above office, which represents nine branches
of the Citizens' Federation in Hongkew and Eastern Areas,
came into existence as a result of a resolution passed at
a joint meeting of these bodies held at Foh Shing Yuen
Restaurant, 152 Canton road on April 7. While ostensibly
subordinate to the Citizens' Federation located in the
Chinese General Chamber of Commerce, this office has assumed
the right to act of its own accord in matters concerning
the nine branches north of the Soochow Creek. Particulars
of the inauguration and resolutions of the association are
contained in the attached appendix.

The association is not governed by rules, the
expenses are not solicited, but issued by the various
branches. Meetings of the Committee are to be held every
Friday at 3 p.m. and the association claims to have 10,000
members at present. The membership fee from $0.20 to
$1.00 is rated according to the size of the shops and
business normally transacted. The association is only
in a position to arbitrate with the landlords on behalf
of the members, and failing to come to a satisfactory
agreement the association is resolved to take necessary
action by submitting the case to the Shanghai Special
District Court.

The various land estate agents concerned declare
that they are willing to waive collection of rentals for the
months of February and March only, providing the arrears of
rents are fully paid off.

The following persons are Standing committee
members of the Association :-

The Movement to Secure Remission of House Rent.
----
The tenants of Passage 157 Avenue Dubail (seven houses)
have written to the "Committee undertaking to secure a
remission of house rents" of the International Settlement,
requesting it to hasten the movement to secure a reduction in
house rents. The monthly rent of each house now
occupied ranges from $70 to $90. Darre Co., 591 Kiangsu Road,
are the collecting agents.
12 members of the Arbitration Section of the Committee
to secure a reduction of house rents (International Settlement)
held a meeting at 6 p.m. April 19 at No. 251 Chefoo Road.
Wang Way Yong (member of the Chinese Chamber of Commerce)
presided.
The following resolutions were passed:-
1) That Chang I Cheng, Yu Hwa Long and Koo Wen Seng
be appointed to arrange a general meeting of representatives.
2) That a reply be sent to the tenants of Passage
157 Avenue Dubail stating that the Committee is taking
measures to settle the question of rent reduction.
3) That the dispute between the tenants and sub-tenants
of Teh Shing Lee, Haining Road, be discussed.

POLICE FORCE
FOR COMMENT
with Lieut. Col.

SHANGHAI PROPERTY OWNERS' ASSOCIATION

16th April, 1932.

The Secretary,
Shanghai Municipal Council,
Shanghai.

Sir,

In view of the agitations reflected by notices
and news items appearing in the Chinese and Foreign Press,
a sample of which appearing in the Sin Wan Pao, April 15,
1932, is enclosed, my Committee desire to bring to your
attention for most earnest consideration, the danger inherent
in continued agitation and publicity of this nature.

This, if allowed to continue, will in all
probability, result in mass refusal to pay rates, taxes
and rent, and may result in physical violence either or
both of which will be subversive of peace and good order
in the Shanghai area.

The Committee request that you take appropriate
steps to avoid such probabilities.

I am, Sir,
Yours faithfully,

(Sgd.) A. W. Buck.
Secretary.
THE SHANGHAI PROPERTY OWNERS' ASSOCIATION.

Regular Meeting of the Committee for Rent Reduction and

The standing committee of this organization met at
3 p.m., day before yesterday for the second time. Nine members
attended the meeting which was presided by Mr. Chu Chen-hua
( 瞿振華 ). The following matters were discussed:-
(1) The Chairman reported regarding the resolutions of
the last meeting.
(2) The drafting committee submitted the constitution of
11 articles with 5 bye-laws and constitution for branch orga-
nizations of 12 articles. After discussion, article by article
they were passed to be printed.
(3) Election of divisional directors - the following 9
were elected: Mr. Yui Tze-ch'eng (於子承), general affairs,

( 毛德潤 ) Miscellaneous affairs, Mr. Liu Yun-sheng ( 劉韻生 )

(4) Refinance of the organization, a resolution was
passed that the money be advanced by the commercial unions.
The French Concession Commercial union contributes $20.00,
Nanyang-Chiao, $10.00, West District $10.00, Tang Kia Wan $10.
Other organizations are to be approached for contributions.

tion. These were passed to be sent to print.

( 敦仁里 ) Rue Brenier de Montmorand, asked for help: Resolved
that (1) the land-lord is to be warned, and (2) a letter be
addressed to the counsel of the landlord to advise the latter
to cease oppressive measures in view of the present conditions.
(7) Mrs. Huang ( 黃氏 ) of 66 Junghua Terrace ( 榮華里 )
same road, asked help: It was considered that the matter
involved legal points and it was decided to forward the matter

该组织常务委员会前天下午3时第二次召开会议。九名成员出席会议，由瞿振華先生主持。讨论了以下事项：

(2) 起草委员会提交了包含11条章程和5条附则的宪章，以及包含12条的分部组织章程。经逐条讨论，通过付印。
(3) 选举各部主任——以下9人当选：於子承先生，总务；盛植人先生，财务；毛德潤先生，杂务；劉韻生先生，会务；葉瑞齋先生，调查；李銘先生，仲裁；張彬秋先生，组织；徐子賢先生，指导；瞿振華先生，社交。

(5) 关于本组织的公开宣言和海报。通过付印。
(6) 蒙托朗布伦尼埃路（Rue Brenier de Montmorand）敦仁里A-1号的賀寰先生请求帮助：决议 (1) 警告房东，(2) 致函房东律师，建议后者鉴于当前局势停止压迫性措施。
(7) 同路榮華里66号的黃氏请求帮助：认为此事涉及法律要点，决定将此事转交

to the voluntary legal advisers and ask Mr. Chen Jui-liu
( 陳瑞麐 ) to take charge.
(8) Jen-shou Terrace ( 仁壽里 ) representative

(9) Haig Terrace representative reported about relief
measures. Resolved, the matter be referred to investigation

(10) Chiu-hsing ( 久興 ), Fu-hai ( 福海 ), Lo-shan

上海市民减租免税运动委员会（ ）于1932年3月19日在直隶路101号花生米业公会举行的会议上，由各公共团体代表成立，详见所附3月21日情报报告摘录副本。该组织的主要发起人是：

朱蔚松（Chu Wei Sung，音译），浙江同乡会主席（连吉里，爱文义路），也是上海各界救国联合会委员（静安寺路91号涌泉坊）。

余华龙（Yui Hwa Loong，音译），市民联合会委员（河南北路上海总商会大楼）兼律师，伯基尔路21号，以及袁洪钟（Yuan Hung Chung，音译），鞋样店业主协会代表，原籍闸北。前抗日救国委员会宣传部重要官员。私下里，他担任该委员会与“奸商”之间的联络官。

该委员会是一个旨在

page_data.en:
2.
persuading the landlords to suspend the collection of rent or
reduce the rentals for premises in the Settlement. This being so,
it is not in a position to force either landlords or tenants to
comply with its proposals. In the event of a landlord insisting
upon collecting the full amount of rent due, the Committee has no
redress but will resort to petitioning the Courts should civil
action be commenced against a tenant, asking the Court to consider
the financial straits of the Shanghai public and render a decision
in favour of the tenant. Letters in this strain have already
been sent to the various Chinese Courts in Shanghai by the Com-
mittee.
Propaganda matter opposing such an action on the part of
local landlords may also be prepared for the local press.
Should a tenant decide that the period of time set by the
Committee for the exemption of rentals or the amount of reduction
of rentals is not sufficient, the Committee will stand aloof.
While no definite decisions have been reached as to the period
of time for which the collection of rentals will be exempted, the
Committees have tentatively decided to advocate the suspension of
the collection of rentals for three months in those districts in
the Settlement north of the Soochow Creek and for two months in
those districts in the Settlement south of the Creek. These
proposals will be submitted to a general meeting of representatives
of local bodies which the Committee hopes to convene in the near
future. The exact date and venue of this meeting are as yet un-
decided.
The Committee is governed by no rules but professes to be a
public spirited body anxious to relieve what it considers to be
the impoverished condition of Settlement residents. While un-
doubtedly having the support of persons who are likely to benefit
from any reduction in rent, the Committee does not appear to be
to any degree representative of either the landlords or the
tenants.
So far the activities of the Committee have been of a nature
page_data.zh:
2.
劝说房东暂停收取或降低租界内房屋的租金。鉴于此，该委员会无权强迫房东或租户遵从其提议。若有房东坚持收取全额到期租金，委员会并无补救办法，但若针对租户提起民事诉讼，委员会将诉诸法院，请求法院考虑上海公众的经济困境，并作出有利于租户的判决。委员会已向上海各中国法院寄送了此类信函。
亦可针对本地房东的此类行为，为本地报刊准备反对宣传材料。
若租户认为委员会设定的免租期或减租幅度不足，委员会将不予介入。虽然对于免收租金的期限尚未作出明确决定，但委员会已初步决定，主张在苏州河以北的租界地区暂停收租三个月，在苏州河以南的租界地区暂停收租两个月。这些提议将提交给由地方团体代表组成的全体会议审议，委员会希望于近期召开此次会议。会议的确切日期和地点尚未确定。
该委员会不受任何规章约束，但自称是一个热心公益的团体，急于缓解其认为的租界居民的贫困状况。虽然无疑得到了可能从任何减租措施中受益的人士的支持，但该委员会似乎并不能在某种程度上代表房东或租户任何一方。
